hints: Focus on each ester link, as every different ester group can break to give an acid part and an alcohol part on hydrolysis.
For compound 1, split both C-O ester bonds and list the acid fragment and alcohol fragment from each side.
Check whether the fragments from the two ends are the same molecule or different molecules, and count only distinct organic products.
walkthrough:
**Recall ester hydrolysis rule**

Think of each ester as acid + alcohol joined together. Hydrolysis adds water across the $\text{C-O}$ bond to remake them.

$$\text{RCOOR' + H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{RCOOH + R'OH}$$

**Analyse compound 1**

Compound 1 is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3$. The left ester gives ethanoic acid plus an alcohol fragment, the right ester gives methanol plus an acid fragment.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH + HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH + CH}_3\text{OH}$$

**Analyse compound 2**

Compound 2 is $\text{CH}_3\text{OOCCH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{COOCH}_3$. Both ends are methyl esters of the same dicarboxylic acid, so both release the same alcohol.

$$\text{dimethyl ester + 2H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{HOOCCH(CH}_3\text{)CH}_2\text{COOH + 2CH}_3\text{OH}$$

**Analyse compound 3 and conclude**

Compound 3 has a cyclic ester (lactone) plus a side-chain ethanoate ester. Opening the ring gives one hydroxy-acid backbone, and the side chain gives ethanoic acid, so the backbone with its two $\text{OH}$ groups counts as one product.

Only compound 1 gives three different organic molecules, so the correct combination is 1 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This claims 1, 2 and 3 all give three products. Compound 2 gives only a dicarboxylic acid plus methanol (2 types) and compound 3 gives only a hydroxy-diol-acid plus ethanoic acid (2 types).
options.B: Incorrect. This claims 1 and 2 both give three products. Compound 2 has two identical methyl ester ends, so hydrolysis produces 2 $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$ plus one diacid, only two different organics.
options.C: Incorrect. This claims 1 and 3 both give three products. Compound 3 on full hydrolysis gives one tri-functional molecule $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(CH}_2\text{OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ plus $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, only two different organics.
options.D: Correct. Only compound 1 gives three different organics: ethanoic acid $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, 3-hydroxypropanoic acid $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, and methanol $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$. Compounds 2 and 3 each give only two different organic products.
